results.title: hypothesis testing - How to choose the test statistic for permutation test? - Cross Validated
results.content: # How to choose the test statistic for permutation test? Is the purpose of permutation test to test the null that several groups of samples come from the same distribution? > The steps in a permutation-based computation of the significance level of a test statistic are as follows:. > i) Choose a test statistic, eg. > ii) Compute the test statistic for the gene of interest,. > iii) Permute the labels on samples at random, and re-compute the test statistic for the rearranged labels; repeat for a large number (perhaps 1,000) permutations, and finally,. What kinds of test statistic should one choose in the first step? But it seems to me that any statistic will work, not necessarily measuring the difference between two groups. These other statistics will be affected differently by the permutation process. If the test statistic is not measuring difference between two groups, then does it still work technically? $\begingroup$ Yes, Tim: you can perform a permutation test on literally any statistic. If you make up some arbitrary statistic you can always do a permutation test and get a p-value, but the meaningfulness of this procedure may be questionable. $\begingroup$ @Tim, the null hypothesis for a permutation test is that the distributions are identical, but there are many ways in which they can be non-identical, some more interesting than others, and the choice of test statistic will have more or less power for different types of non-identical. You choose a test statistic that measures what you're interested in/has the properties you need. If you want to compare means, you base it on differences of means; if you want a robust comparison of location, you measure something else; if you want to compare standard deviations, you use a statistic that does that; if you want to compare the whole distribution you use a statistic that compares distributions (such as a k-sample version of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, for an example). 12") Permutation tests: criteria to choose a test statistic. 2") Permutation test for multiple correlation test statistics. 4") Selection of test statistic for permutation test of variability. 1") Permutation test and wilcoxon rank-sum test giving different results.
